back_translation: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

A man to whom God gives riches, possessions, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not give him the power to eat of them — instead a stranger eats them. This too is without substance, and a grievous affliction.

If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, however many the days of his years may be, but his soul is not satisfied with good things, and he does not even receive a burial — I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
For that child comes in without substance and departs in darkness, and its name is covered in darkness.
Though it never saw the sun and never knew anything, that child has more rest than that man.
And even if that man lives a thousand years twice over but does not enjoy what is good — do not all go to the same place?
All a man's toil is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
For what advantage has the wise man over the fool? And what does the poor man gain who knows how to conduct himself before the people?
What the eyes see is better than the wandering of desire. This too is without substance, a chasing after the wind.
Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; he cannot go to law against one mightier than himself.
For the more words there are, the more they increase what is without substance — and what profit is that to anyone?

For who knows what is good for a man in this life, throughout the few short days of his life without substance, which he passes through like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will happen after him under the sun?
